title: 1955 Estonian Supreme Soviet election
text: Elections to the Supreme Soviet of the Estonian SSR were held on 27 February 1955. As was the case with the two previous elections of the Estonian SSR, the Bloc of Communists and Non-Party Candidates was the only party permitted to contest the elections, and won all 125 seats.

title: 1955 Soviet Union regional elections
text: On February 27, 1955, elections were held for the Supreme Soviets of the Soviet Union's constituent republics. According to Soviet law, 3,369,000 out of an eligible adult voting population of 123,174,000 were disenfranchised for various reasons.

title: Belgrade declaration
text: The Belgrade declaration is a document signed by President of Yugoslavia Josip Broz Tito and Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev on 2 June 1955 that brought about a short reconciliation between the two states. Negotiations leading up to the signing of the document took place between 27 May and 2 June.

title: Władysław Gomułka initiates talks about the Repatriation of Poles (1955–59).
text: Władysław Gomułka was a Polish communist politician. He was the de facto leader of post-war Poland from 1956 to 1970.

title: The first Soviet hydrogen bomb, RDS-37, is tested.
text: RDS-37 was the Soviet Union's first two-stage thermonuclear weapon test, dropped from a Tupolev Tu-16 bomber over Semipalatinsk Test Site on 22 November 1955. The yield was 1.6 megatons, scaled down from a 3 megaton design.

title: The 1st Soviet Antarctic Expedition begins.
text: The First Soviet Antarctic Expedition was a 1955–1957 expedition to Antarctica by explorers from the Soviet Union, led by Mikhail Somov.

title: The Pospelov Commission is set up.
text: The Pospelov Commission was a commission of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union Presidium. It was headed by Pyotr Pospelov, whose findings had laid the basis and the contents of Nikita Khrushchev's "secret speech" On the Personality Cult and its Consequences.
